## Perfect on my computer…

{{< stepper file="examples/l04_too_long.py" >}}

::: {.notes}
Open with the problem: "Here's a banner with the name inside the box. It looks perfect on my computer. Watch what happens with a longer name." Press Run all. "Today we fix this properly."
:::

## Values inside text

```{.python code-line-numbers="|1|2"}
name = "LAB-PC-14"
print(f"Name: {name}")
```

::: {.fragment}
- `f` before the quotation mark: an **f-string**
- `{ }` is a hole, filled with the value inside it
- Everything else prints exactly as typed
:::

::: {.notes}
TEACHER PROMPT (first use of f-strings): "The f before the quotation mark makes this an f-string, short for formatted string. Inside it, curly braces are holes; Python fills each with the value of what's inside. Everything outside the braces prints exactly as typed, spaces included. No commas, no sep: what you see is what you get."
:::

## Padding

```{.python code-line-numbers="2"}
cpu = "arm64"
print(f"[{cpu:<8}]")
```

::: {.fragment}
- `:<8` take up **8 characters**, value on the **left**
- `:>8` value on the right · `:^8` centred
- The arrow points where the value goes
:::

::: {.notes}
TEACHER PROMPT (first use of padding): "After the variable, a colon starts the format. <8 means take up 8 characters with the value on the left; the rest is spaces. > puts it on the right, ^ centres it. The square brackets aren't special: they let us see the spaces."
:::

## Predict, then step

{{< stepper file="examples/l04_fstring_report.py" >}}

::: {.notes}
About 10 minutes. Students write the exact output first. Ask: lines 7 and 8 look almost the same; what will each print? After line 8: "No f, so no holes. The braces print as ordinary characters. The most common f-string mistake, and Python doesn't warn you: a logic error."
:::

## Padding inside a box

{{< stepper file="examples/l04_padding.py" >}}

::: {.notes}
Ask: the top line is 30 characters. Show line 8 is too (1 + 28 + 1). Where does 18 come from on line 9? (10 characters before the hole, 2 after: 30 − 12.) Then go back to the "too long" slide: does Python cut the name off? TEACHER PROMPT: "Padding only ever adds spaces; it never cuts a value short. Pick a width bigger than any value you expect: slightly too wide looks fine, too narrow breaks."
:::

## Same output. Which would you rather read?

```python
a = platform.node()
b = platform.system()
x2 = platform.python_version()
print(f"{a:<12}{b:<12}{x2}")
```

```python
# One row of a lab inventory. Columns are 12 wide so rows line up.
computer_name = platform.node()
os_name = platform.system()
python_version = platform.python_version()
print(f"{computer_name:<12}{os_name:<12}{python_version}")
```

::: {.notes}
TEACHER PROMPT (naming and comments): "Code is read far more often than it's written: by your teacher, a classmate, and you in three weeks. Python doesn't care what you call a variable. People do. A good name says what the value is; a good comment says why." Python names: lowercase with underscores. Ask: why can't a name have a space in it?
:::

## Modify

1. Put the name and OS **inside** the box, padded
2. Centre the title with `:^`
3. Make the box 4 characters wider

```{pyodide}
import platform

name = platform.node()
system = platform.system()

print("+============================+")
print("|       SYSTEM BANNER        |")
print("+============================+")
print("Name:", name)
print("System:", system)
```
